cards.text: It's Passover night, and Jesus is at the table with His apostles. He's just told them the hand of His betrayer is right there on the table with His. So they start asking each other which of them could ever do it.
Then the talk at that table takes a turn. A dispute breaks out among the disciples.

cards.question: At the Passover table, a dispute breaks out among the disciples. What is it about?

answers.text: Which of them should be considered the greatest
Which of them should lead the Passover prayer
Which of them should go out to buy supplies

cards.text: I once argued with the dead batteries in my junk drawer over which of us was the most useful, and friend, we were ALL in the drawer. Then Jesus steps in: the kings of the Gentiles lord it over them, and those in authority call themselves benefactors.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples they should be like the kings of the Gentiles.

cards.text: Instead, Jesus flips the whole ladder upside down. The greatest among them should be like the youngest.

cards.question: Jesus says the one who leads should be like the one who ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks who's greater, the one who reclines at the table or the one who serves. And He answers it Himself: “Is it not the one who reclines?”

cards.question: Jesus says the one who reclines at the table is greater than the one who serves. So how does He describe Himself among the disciples?

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to them. They're the ones, He says, who have stood by Him in His trials.

cards.question: Jesus bestows a kingdom on the disciples, just as His ___ has bestowed one on Him.
Jesus bestows a kingdom on the disciples. What does He say they'll do in His kingdom?

answers.text: Eat and drink at His table
Guard the gates of the city

cards.text: A table in His kingdom? My mustache just stood straight up, friend, and there's more: they'll sit on thrones.

cards.question: From those thrones in the kingdom, the disciples will be judging the ___ tribes of Israel.

cards.text: Then Jesus speaks to Simon Peter, one of the Twelve. “Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift all of you like wheat.”

cards.question: Satan has asked to sift the disciples like wheat. What has Jesus done for Simon?

answers.text: Prayed that his faith will not fail
Sent an angel to stand guard over him
Told him to hide until morning comes

cards.text: And Jesus gives Simon a job. When he has turned back, he's to strengthen his brothers.

cards.question: Peter answers Jesus right away. How far does he say he's ready to go with Him?

answers.text: Even to prison and to death
All the way back to Galilee
As far as the city of Jericho

cards.text: Prison AND death, no pause, and friend, I can't even commit to a new topping that fast! But Jesus answers Peter with a word about a rooster.

cards.question: Jesus tells Peter the rooster will not crow today until Peter has denied ___ times that he knows Him.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks them all a question. Back when He sent them out without purse or bag or sandals, did they lack anything?

cards.question: Jesus asks if the disciples lacked anything when He sent them out without purse or bag or sandals. What do they answer?

cards.text: Nothing! I had a whole junk drawer full of stuff and still lacked everything, friend. But now, Jesus tells them, things are different.

cards.question: Now Jesus tells the one with a purse to leave it behind.
Jesus says the one without a sword should sell his ___ and buy one.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them this Scripture must be fulfilled in Him: “And He was numbered with the transgressors.”

cards.question: Jesus says what is written about Him is reaching its fulfillment.

cards.text: The disciples speak up. They've got something to show Jesus.

cards.question: The disciples say, Look Lord, here are ___ swords.
The disciples show Jesus two swords. What does He answer?

cards.text: And that's where the table talk ends for now. But friend, this night is just getting started.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new event in Papa Dorin's drawer backstory: he argued with the dead batteries over which of them was the most useful. The backstory has the batteries arguing among themselves over who had the most charge left. It never has Papa Dorin arguing with them about usefulness. Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery, not new drawer events.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: "My mustache just stood straight up" is a mild reaction, not a real laugh. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant, at a moment (thrones in His kingdom) that could hold a stronger line. It also leans on the mustache as the gag.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: "Peter answers Jesus right away" adds a time the text doesn't give. Luke 22:33 doesn't say how quickly Peter answers. Card 5's "no pause" repeats the added timing as a description of Peter, not as Papa Dorin's own exaggeration.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers are travel destinations ("All the way back to Galilee", "As far as the city of Jericho"). The right answer, "Even to prison and to death", is a different kind of thing and is far weightier, so it stands out right away.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "I had a whole junk drawer full of stuff and still lacked everything" doesn't click. The drawer's contents weren't his, and lacking "everything" while surrounded by stuff doesn't match the action in the verse: being sent out with nothing and lacking nothing. A baker would likely say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Story card 12 already tells the baker that this Scripture "must be fulfilled in Him." That all but gives away the true-or-false answer on card 13 (what is written about Him is reaching its fulfillment), leaving nothing to reason out.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
